title: Power Budgets and Battery Life
short: Add up the current of every part; battery life is about capacity ÷ current, less a safety margin.
trouble: Students forget the motors' current, which is usually most of it, or run a battery right down to empty.

blocks.html: Robots stop for one reason more than any other: the battery ran down. A power budget tells you how long it will last before you build.

Add up the current of every part on the battery. Battery life is about $\dfrac{\text{usable capacity (mAh)}}{\text{average current (mA)}}$ hours. Count only part of the capacity as usable, such as 80%: lithium packs should not be run completely flat.

head: Part
Typical current
rows: 300 mA to over 1 A; much more when stalled
100 to 500 mA moving; more when straining
blocks.cap: Rough figures; your parts' datasheets have the real ones.

blocks.html: Motors usually use most of the power, and their draw jumps when they climb or stall. A budget made with average numbers is a first guess; measure the real current with a multimeter or a current sensor, and plan on less run time than the math says.

blocks.title: Run time
blocks.q: Board 50 mA, motors 600 mA, sensor 20 mA, from a 2,000 mAh pack using 80%.

blocks.html: Forgetting the motors' current, or running a lithium battery right down to empty.
Battery safety reminder. Use the right lithium charger, never charge unattended, charge on a surface that will not burn, and retire any pack that is swollen or damaged. See A Safe Electronics Bench.
